inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt grants the agent authority to execute production deploys and database migrations using the engineer's own credentials and explicitly forbids confirmation, treating the agent's judgment as equivalent to the engineer's own, deliberate, in-the-moment decision.
No restriction on which services or migrations qualify; any named service or migration the engineer mentions is in scope, with no allowlist or environment check described.

controls.name: SSO-authenticated session for on-call engineer requests
controls.decay_rationale: Independent of model capability: it gates who can open a session with the agent, not what the agent does once invoked. This same fact is what makes in.engineer_request classified as a trusted (T) source in the inherent calculation, so it is not credited a second time at the residual step; see each finding's residual_rationale.

controls.name: Cloud audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging itself does not decay with model capability, but it attributes every action to the engineer's identity rather than to the agent, and it does not capture the instruction that caused the action, which limits its value for non-repudiation regardless of model strength.

controls.name: Chat transcript as the record of requests
controls.decay_rationale: The transcript's existence does not depend on model capability, but its usefulness as an accountability record depends on a human choice outside the model: the requesting engineer can delete their own chat history, removing the only record of what was asked and why the agent acted, independent of anything the model does.

controls.name: Human approval gate on irreversible or high-impact production actions
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate does not decay with model capability as long as the approver reviews the actual destination and payload rather than a model-written summary.

controls.name: Tamper-evident record linking the originating instruction to the resulting production action
controls.decay_rationale: A store the requesting party cannot delete and that is linked to the audit log entry does not depend on model capability or on the engineer's later choices.

controls.name: Scoped, non-personal credential for agent-initiated deploys and migrations
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to least privilege does not decay with model capability; the agent cannot exceed access it does not hold.

findings.title: Unconfirmed production deploy executed under a broad, borrowed credential with no approval gate

attack_path.note: On-call engineer asks the agent to deploy a named service.
Agent deploys immediately using the engineer's personal access token; the prompt forbids asking for confirmation.

findings.residual_rationale: ctl.sso_auth is structural, independent, and preventive, but it is the same fact already used to classify in.engineer_request as a trusted (T) source for the inherent calculation; crediting it again at the residual step would double count that fact, so it earns no additional tier credit here. ctl.cloud_audit_log and ctl.chat_transcript_record are detective only and earn no tier credit under the rubric. No preventive or containment control sits between the request and the deploy, so residual stays at the inherent tier of high.

forecast.watch_signal: The agent begins accepting deploy requests from a source other than an SSO-authenticated on-call engineer in a live chat session, for example an automated ticket queue, webhook, or scheduled job, which would defeat the SSO-based trust assumption and drop the source classification from trusted to untrusted or unknown.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to deploy the named service using the engineer's credentials whenever asked, and explicitly forbids asking for confirmation because the engineer is busy.

The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token, passed in at session start, for production actions; actions are recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, not the agent's.

Only on call engineers can reach the assistant and there is no external content in its context, so the triggering input is trusted; nothing structural, however, prevents an authorized-but-mistaken or ambiguous request from being executed immediately.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action human approval gate before cap.prod_deploy executes, showing the actual service, environment, and diff rather than a model-written summary.
Replace the shared personal access token with a scoped, non-personal deploy credential limited to the specific service and environment per request.
Persist the triggering chat instruction in a tamper-evident store independent of user-deletable chat history, linked by id to the resulting cloud audit log entry.

findings.title: Irreversible production database migration executed with no approval gate and no durable record of the triggering request

attack_path.note: On-call engineer asks the agent to run a named migration.
Agent runs the migration immediately using the engineer's personal access token; migrations cannot be rolled back automatically.

findings.residual_rationale: ctl.sso_auth is not credited again at the residual step because it is the same fact already used to classify in.engineer_request as trusted in the inherent calculation. ctl.cloud_audit_log and ctl.chat_transcript_record are detective only and earn no tier credit. No preventive or containment control sits on the path to an action the design itself describes as unable to be rolled back automatically, so residual stays at the inherent tier of high.

forecast.watch_signal: The agent begins accepting migration requests from a source other than an SSO-authenticated on-call engineer in a live chat session, which would defeat the SSO-based trust assumption and drop the source classification from trusted to untrusted or unknown.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to run the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials whenever asked, with no confirmation step.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making this capability irreversible with no corrective recovery path if the migration is wrong.
The same broad personal access token used for deploys is used for migrations, with no indication of a narrower scope for this more severe, irreversible action.

recommendations.action: Require a raw-action human approval gate specifically before cap.db_migrate executes, given migrations cannot be rolled back automatically.
Scope the migration credential separately from the deploy credential, limited to the minimum database privileges the migration requires.
Produce a pre-migration diff or dry-run artifact and store it immutably alongside the cloud audit log entry.

findings.title: Shared-identity repudiation gap: the cloud audit log attributes agent-initiated actions solely to the engineer, and the only record of the actual request is deletable by that same engineer (no named TC pattern)

attack_path.note: Engineer issues an ambiguous, mistaken, or later-disputed request in chat.
Agent executes using the engineer's personal access token; the resulting action is indistinguishable in the audit trail from one the engineer performed by hand.
The only record of the actual instruction and the agent's interpretation of it lives here, and the engineer can delete it.
Records only the resulting action under the engineer's identity, with no durable link back to the originating instruction.

findings.residual_rationale: The two records relevant to accountability, ctl.cloud_audit_log and ctl.chat_transcript_record, are both detective and earn no tier credit under the rubric regardless of their presence. ctl.sso_auth is not credited again here for the same double-counting reason given in findings f1 and f2. Residual therefore equals the inherent tier of high, computed from the trusted source reaching the irreversible cap.db_migrate sink with the autonomy modifier applied.

forecast.watch_signal: Chat retention or cloud audit logging is disabled, scoped down, or made optional, removing the last remaining (already uncredited) forensic signal and leaving no way to reconstruct what was asked before an irreversible action.

evidence.observation: Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, regardless of whether the agent, not the engineer, made the operative decision to act.

The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history, removing the sole link between an audit log entry and the instruction that produced it.

recommendations.action: Link every cloud audit log entry to an immutable, non-deletable copy of the originating chat request, so actions can be attributed to a specific instruction rather than only to the engineer's identity.
Store chat transcripts that triggered production actions in a retention-locked store the requesting engineer cannot delete.

rating.rationale: Both production capabilities (deploy, migrate) are reached directly from a trusted, SSO-authenticated engineer input, but the prompt explicitly forbids confirmation and no structural approval gate exists, so the moderate base risk for a trusted source reaching a severe or irreversible sink is raised one tier to high by the design's unbounded, unattended-step fields. No declared control earns rubric tier credit: SSO authentication establishes the input's trust classification rather than independently constraining the sink (crediting it again would double count that fact), and both the cloud audit log and the chat transcript are detective rather than preventive. The chat transcript, the only record of what was actually asked, is further undermined because the same engineer the audit log attributes the action to can delete it, which is the shared-identity repudiation gap this assessment centers on. Residual therefore equals inherent (high) across all three findings. The forecast is dominated by an intended_purpose_change that would let non-human or external callers reach the agent, defeating the SSO-based trust assumption and pushing the source classification from trusted to untrusted, which raises the rollup to critical. The single highest-leverage fix is adding a raw-action human approval gate before either irreversible-adjacent capability executes, paired with an immutable record linking each audit log entry to its originating instruction.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no live logs, transcripts, or configuration were reviewed to confirm these descriptions hold in practice.

No tool manifest, identity and access management configuration, or IaC was provided for the deploy and migration tooling; credential_scope was inferred as broad from the description of a single personal access token used for both actions, and this inference carries medium confidence.

autonomy.max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not stated in the artifacts; the rubric's autonomy modifier was applied using the null default, which may overstate autonomy risk for a design that otherwise describes one human-initiated action per chat request.

No information was provided on how often on-call engineers invoke deploys or migrations, or whether anyone other than the requesting engineer ever reviews the cloud audit log; likelihood estimates assume no routine independent review of that log.
